ready.note: set in app.js armNext() after the first painted frame. The fonts clause is load-bearing: each frame opens a cold page, and a capture taken before the serif arrives rasterises every label in the fallback font — globe-default moved 1.016% on 2026-08-06 and the diff was nothing but label halos and reflowed voyage lists.

frames.name: descent
frames.note: The near field at 700 m: displaced water, the near/far seam and the horizon, off the Bristol Channel. ⚠ ITS NOTE USED TO CLAIM "the Great Western at true scale" AND NO HULL HAS EVER BEEN IN IT — checked pixelwise against the 2026-08-03 baseline on 2026-08-04: zero hull-dark pixels in either. The descent path does call psgFleet, so a hull within 182 km should draw; it does not, and that is an open bug rather than a framing accident. Until it is fixed this frame watches WATER, and nothing here defends the near-field fleet.

frames.name: descent-high
frames.note: Nine kilometres: just ABOVE the handover, so the token side of the seam is watched too. A frame on only one side of a boundary cannot see the boundary move. ⚠ Do not re-point this one northward — 51.1N 3.87W is over Exmoor and the frame comes back a near-black picture of unlit ground.

frames.name: descent-coast
frames.note: The near-field GROUND: the Strait of Gibraltar at 260 m, looking south at the Moroccan coast. The globe sphere is 192x128 — a 209 km facet — so at this eye height the backdrop is a flat plate with a polygon edge for a horizon and can never show a coast. This frame watches the displaced land patch that can.

frames.name: aboard
frames.note: ABOARD: the close-up, entered the way a viewer enters it — by naming a ship. This view is what the project is most often asked about and it had no baseline at all, for the plain reason that no URL could ask for it. Watches the true-scale hull, the near-field water it floats in, her wake, and the join between that water and the globe behind it.

frames.name: aboard-off
frames.note: ABOARD, a different era and hull: the container ship on the Asia-Europe run. Two frames rather than one because the close-up has to hold for a 400 m motor ship and a 72 m paddle steamer, and a single frame cannot see that.

frames.name: map-floor
frames.note: THE MAP AT ITS LOWEST — 300 km over Cape St Vincent, with the treasure fleet homeward bound and the Portuguese coast in the same frame. 300 km is where the token exaggeration peaks and therefore where the wheel now stops: below it the ramp unwinds the token toward true scale and the ship SHRANK, from 65 km long at 35.6% of the frame to 100 m at 2%. Watches the ship-to-coast proportion, which is the thing being asserted, and the water at that height.

frames.name: aboard-coast
frames.note: ABOARD, CLOSE INSHORE — the Athenian armada five kilometres off the Peloponnese, with land 121 m high and the sun 65 degrees up. August reported seeing NO LAND from the close-up while the map showed the ship hugging a coast, and no frame watched it: `aboard` and `aboard-off` both happen to sit in open water, and the first attempt at this frame put the guano clipper a thousand kilometres off Chile. Chosen by sweeping every ship in every era at the frozen instant for the one nearest to lit land, rather than by guessing.

frames.name: sea-magnified
frames.note: OPEN WATER AT 10 km — magnified far past the scale the sea shader was tuned for, which is the band between the near-field handover at 8 km and the old 12 km map floor. August photographed a regular lattice of pale dashes here and no frame watched it: every other water frame is either at globe zoom or in the near field. The cause was foam laid along the crests of a FOUR-component Gerstner sum — four sinusoids are visibly periodic once resolved, and white on their crests draws that periodicity. Measured by FFT: one component at 33 px, peak-to-mean 395, now 139.

frames.name: aboard-carrier
frames.note: ABOARD, THE CARRIER — the strike group on deployment. Added round 35 with the paint rebuild: she read as a black cutout in both views (deck 0x23272b, island 0x2b3036, topside #4e545b — soot albedos tuned to rigs). Watches the measured scheme — FS 26270 haze-grey verticals, weathered non-skid deck — and the deck markings, deck park and island against the reference relative pattern: island brightest, deck ~0.9×, shell 0.2–0.6×.

frames.name: aboard-titanic
frames.note: ABOARD, THE LINER — Titanic on her maiden-voyage track. Added round 34 with the era profile rebuild: black shell to B deck with the white house above, forecastle/poop breaks, 9.46° raked buff funnels and masts whose trucks stand 62.5 m over the load line. The Sea view is where the r32 era-dress and this structure meet; no baseline watched a liner here before.

frames.name: aboard-yamato
frames.note: ABOARD, THE BATTLESHIP — Yamato on the Ten-ichi-go sortie. Added round 36 with her second detail pass: the 1941 close-in fit (eight shielded 25 mm triples on bandstands), searchlight platforms winged off the pagoda, stowage hatches on the quarterdeck and two floatplanes aft — one riding the port catapult. Watches the crowded amidships silhouette the record describes.
